quarterly_data.quarter: Southern Company regulatory filing: Georgia Power Large Load Economic Development Report Q2 2026 (08-17-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Georgia Power's quarterly large-load report to the Georgia PSC (period ending June 30, 2026): the portfolio of large load customers committed to receiving service from Georgia Power (Contracts for Electric Service plus Requests for Electric Service) grew by 3,200 MW to a total of 15,600 MW across 32 customers through the mid-2030s; near-term commitments for the winter of 2028/2029 rose from 7,800 MW in Q1 2026 to 8,700 MW. Twenty-one of the 32 committed projects have broken ground and eleven are pending construction; load that has broken ground held steady at 8,500 MW of the 15,600 MW (6,800 MW of the 8,700 MW near-term). Georgia Power says these customers are materializing and making progress 'without material delays'. Since the 2023 IRP Update, customer commitments expanded from 3,600 MW to 15,600 MW. The project list is dominated by projects classed Data Center/Crypto (customer names redacted).
quarterly_data.figure: Committed large load 15,600 MW across 32 customers (+3,200 MW); near-term (winter 2028/2029) 8,700 MW (from 7,800 MW); broken ground 8,500 MW; 21 broken ground, 11 pending

quarterly_data.quarter: Southern Company regulatory filing: Georgia Power Large Load Economic Development Report Q2 2026 (08-17-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Georgia Power's economic development pipeline as of June 30, 2026: the total pipeline through the mid-2030s rose from 76,200 MW to 84,800 MW (+8,600 MW), of which 80,100 MW are large load economic development projects; large load projects rose by a net 6,900 MW (6,800 MW entered the pipeline, a net 1,500 MW increase from projects that modified their projected load, 1,400 MW exited). For the near term (winter 2028/2029) the total pipeline held steady at 26,200 MW while the large load pipeline decreased by 1,400 MW to 22,200 MW, which the company attributes primarily to changes in projected near-term load ramps, partially offset by net project additions. Since the 2023 IRP Update the total pipeline expanded from approximately 17,000 MW to approximately 84,800 MW. Georgia Power says the latest data continue to support its projection of robust economic growth and the timing of new large load customers.
quarterly_data.figure: Total pipeline 84,800 MW (from 76,200 MW); large load pipeline 80,100 MW (net +6,900 MW); near-term large load pipeline 22,200 MW (down 1,400 MW)
